entries.note:
A capture reuses the declared-command runner (no shell, cwd = root, 10 s / 8 MiB), requires the PNG signature **before touching disk**, creates `into` after a LEXICAL boundary check and confines its realpath afterwards, then writes the image and the manifest through temp-and-rename; a same-millisecond collision gets a numeric suffix.

The ORDER is the contract, and the record (`orchestrator/tests/capture-corpus.json`) holds the capture directory after every case because of it: a refusal promises that nothing was written, and only what is on disk can check that promise. Two consequences of the order are easy to 'fix' into bugs — the directory is created before the path is resolved, so `into` naming an existing FILE refuses with the filesystem's own EEXIST and no route status; and the lexical check runs before anything is created, so it must not be replaced with a resolve (which would follow a symlink and refuse differently, after creating nothing). A manifest this workspace cannot read is replaced rather than fatal: the capture a person just took is not lost to a file something else wrote badly.
